issues.body: `char_sets_complete_for` sorts each key but neither rejects nor deduplicates repeated predicates within one `CharSet`. Consequently `{p}` and `{p,p}` compare as distinct keys although they denote the same exact predicate set, while `char_set_has` counts each entry once. Supplying `{p}` plus `{p,p}`, and `{q}` plus `{q,q}`, with balanced `distinct_subjects` totals and no served `{p,q}` cohort can make both completeness checks pass. Rule C2 may then mark the same-source pairing dead and prune a combination that can contribute. `duplicate_char_sets_decline_the_prune` tests repeated identical vectors only, so it does not exercise the prior-round counterexample.
issues.fix_hint: Canonicalize every key as a mathematical set before checking repeated keys, or fail closed if any `CharSet` contains a duplicate predicate. Add a non-vacuous negative test using `{p}`, `{p,p}`, `{q}`, and `{q,q}` with balanced totals and no served co-occurrence key; assert that no dead pairing, candidate prune, or dead-combination verdict is emitted.
issues.title: Duplicate predicates within a characteristic-set key still bypass the completeness guard

verdict.summary: The round-four major recall-safety defect remains. The new guard rejects duplicate sorted vectors but still treats a characteristic-set key as a list rather than a mathematical predicate set: `{p}` and `{p,p}` remain different keys. Since `char_set_has` counts each characteristic-set entry once regardless of repeated predicates inside it, balanced `{p}`/`{p,p}` and `{q}`/`{q,q}` entries can satisfy both completeness equalities while omitting the live `{p,q}` cohort. Rule C2 may then report the same-source pairing dead and suppress a contributing combination. The added test again covers repeated identical keys, not this counterexample. Progress is stagnant.
